intro: Ask one question at a time, then stay quiet and let them talk. You will not use all 20: pick the ones that fit this person. A kind "not yet" is a good result too.

steps.aim: Learn how they practice and why they applied, before you talk about the program.

qs.ask: How do you practice now: in a Mysore room, in led classes, or alone? How many days a week?
qs.listen: Primary Series by heart, plus Mysore and led class? That is the entry level.
qs.why: Checks the entry level before anything else.
qs.original: (added by us: entry check)

qs.ask: What has kept you practicing all these years, when many people stop?
qs.listen: Habit, a teacher, or only new asana? This shows what keeps them going.
qs.why: Opens warmly and tests our habit idea in their life.
qs.original: Why haven't you given up on this goal?

qs.ask: What changed recently in your practice or teaching that made you apply?
qs.listen: A real event, like a stuck practice or students who stop coming.
qs.why: A real trigger shows a real need, not only curiosity.
qs.original: What's changed that makes you consider doing something now?

qs.ask: What is the hardest thing in your practice or your teaching right now?
qs.listen: One clear, real problem, or only a wish to learn more asana?
qs.why: Hears their problem in their own words, before any program talk.
qs.original: What's the biggest challenge you're dealing with right now?

steps.aim: Get real stories and details, so you see if this program can help.

qs.ask: Can you tell me about one real time this problem happened, in practice or class?
qs.listen: A true story with details, not a general idea.
qs.why: A real story is clearer than a general answer through a translator.
qs.original: Can you give me an example?

qs.ask: If you teach: what happens in your classes that you wish did not happen?
qs.listen: Students who stop coming back? Write down their exact words.
qs.why: For teachers and studio owners: opens the problem of students leaving.
qs.original: What's happening that you wish wasn't?

qs.ask: What have you already tried: workshops, trips to Mysore, other teachers, changes in your classes?
qs.listen: What failed and why. Is this program truly different from what they tried?
qs.why: If we are not different from what failed, say so.
qs.original: What have you tried so far?

qs.ask: Of all you told me, which part is hardest to change on your own?
qs.listen: We can be their teacher for 30 days. We cannot give them time.
qs.why: Shows if a teacher is the missing piece, or something else.
qs.original: Which part feels the hardest to solve?

steps.aim: Let them name what is not working now. Ask gently, never push on pain.

qs.ask: If your daily practice stays just as it is, what will that mean for you?
qs.listen: Real worry, or real peace. If peace, they may not need this.
qs.why: A calm answer lets a lead see they do not need us.
qs.original: What happens if nothing changes?

qs.ask: If you teach: if you teach the same way for years, what happens to your students?
qs.listen: Do students stay or leave? If most stay, the need may be small.
qs.why: For teachers and studio owners: the core question of students who stay.
qs.original: What's the price of continuing down the same path?

qs.ask: What would make this problem important enough that you want to change it?
qs.listen: If nothing would, this may not be the time. Do not push.
qs.why: Lets them see on their own if now is the time.
qs.original: At what point does staying the same become unacceptable?

steps.aim: Hear the practice they want, and check if 30 days can serve it.

qs.ask: What kind of practitioner, or teacher, do you want to become?
qs.listen: Deep practice over years, or a title? This program gives no authorization.
qs.why: Finds people who want a title, which this program never gives.
qs.original: What kind of person do you want to become?

qs.ask: If you joined, how would you know a year later that it really helped?
qs.listen: Real signs, like a steady daily practice, not a new asana or title.
qs.why: Their answer shows if their hopes match what 30 days give.
qs.original: How would you know you'd succeeded?

steps.aim: Find real reasons to say no: life, body, time, or a better choice.

qs.ask: What would need to change so you can be away from home and work for 30 days?
qs.listen: A real plan, or a sign this is not the right time.
qs.why: Checks if their life truly has room for 30 days away.
qs.original: What specifically would need to change for the timing to work?

qs.ask: What worries you about joining: an injury, the way we teach, or something else?
qs.listen: Injury or the method. Answer with facts, and promise nothing about the body.
qs.why: Brings injuries and worries out early, so you answer with facts.
qs.original: What risks would you want to understand before committing?

qs.ask: What other teachers, trips, or courses are you thinking about for your practice?
qs.listen: Other good choices. If another teacher fits them better, say so.
qs.why: Shows we filter, not chase. Honesty here protects the brand.
qs.original: What alternatives are you considering?

qs.ask: What would make 30 days of Mysore with us the wrong step for you?
qs.listen: Real reasons to say no. If one is strong, let them go kindly.
qs.why: The clearest way for a lead to see they should not join.
qs.original: What would make this the wrong solution for you?

steps.aim: Give your honest view and let them choose yes, no, or wait.

qs.ask: We watched your practice video. Would you like our honest view, even if it is 'not yet'?
qs.listen: Are they open to 'not yet'? Then give the real view, kindly.
qs.why: Shows a teacher who notices, which is what we really offer.
qs.original: Would you like my honest recommendation?

qs.ask: What do you still need to know or do before you can decide?
qs.listen: The real reason they wait, and a reply date they choose themselves.
qs.why: No false urgency. They set the next step, not us.
qs.original: Is there anything stopping you from making a decision today?

qs.ask: Which is right for you: joining this group, waiting, or not joining?
qs.listen: Yes, no and wait are equal. If yes, explain the payment steps.
qs.why: A calm, open close. 'Wait' is an equal answer.
qs.original: Does it make sense to get started?

never_say: "Only today", "last seats", or any deadline that is not real.
Calling this program teacher training, authorization or certification. It gives a certificate of completion, not authorization.
Any promise of results: a new asana, more students, "your students will stay", or a healed injury.
"Investment", "it pays for itself", or "you can't afford to miss this".
Anything that makes Boonchu's authorization bigger than it is.
"Let me know soon", or contacting them again and again after the call.
